note.question: Can competing firms credibly tell consumers which attribute is important even when each firm may benefit from emphasizing the attribute on which its own product performs better?
note.overview: The paper is an explicit two-sender cheap-talk game. Competing firms privately observe noisy signals about which product attribute matters, send nonverifiable messages, and anticipate a consumer's costly search and purchase response; equilibrium credibility is the central object.

components.label: Perfect Bayesian equilibrium of a two-sender cheap-talk game

Strategies specify signal-contingent messages and posterior-contingent consumer search and purchase. components.label: Model sequence and system structure
components.explanation: Nature determines which of two product attributes is more important. Each firm privately observes an independently noisy signal about that state. The firms simultaneously send nonverifiable messages h or l. The consumer observes both messages, updates beliefs, and decides whether to pay search cost c to learn product-specific idiosyncratic values.
